findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_opportunity, get_upgrade_link, deadline_calendar, search_foundations, list_saved_searches, save_search · Private data: search_grants_and_procurement, search_grantsplus, whats_new, get_tool_guide, search_foundations, get_foundation, find_funders_of, funders_for_cause, check_connection · Public sink: list_saved_searches, save_search · Destructive: search_grantsplus, search_procurement, list_saved_searches, delete_saved_search, update_saved_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_opportunity, get_upgrade_link, deadline_calendar, search_foundations, list_saved_searches, save_search · Private data: search_grants_and_procurement, search_grantsplus, whats_new, get_tool_guide, search_foundations, get_foundation, find_funders_of, funders_for_cause, check_connection · Public sink: list_saved_searches, save_search · Destructive: search_grantsplus, search_procurement, list_saved_searches, delete_saved_search, update_saved_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_grants_and_procurement" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
